utterances.text: You said that since you had no weapons, you just went back home to Gruz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, which unit had you been assigned to on the 31st of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To no unit. I said that I had not been in the army by the 31st of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about from then on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, later on in March or April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you, in which unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 163rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ZNG?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this 163rd Brigade of the Croatian army deployed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the specific positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at the island of Lokrum. I'm sorry, on Kolocep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other elements of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, on the -- in October and November, did you transport food up to the positions of the Croatian army on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We didn't drive a transport food there. We once brought it up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In November at some point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you specify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 10th, the 15th of November; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you go up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once. It was only this one day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get through all the way to Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We walked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do this together with Tonci Skocko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who with, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were other civilians there who were assisting, who came to help on that day. Maybe the next day it was someone else. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where from were you taking this food? Who tasked you with this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's up towards the Old Town, towards Sipsin. It's near Glavica. We would take it up as far as there by van, and since the road was blocked on all sides, you had to carry it up the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one man enough to take the food up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say only one man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe five, six, ten of us. Seven, ten, I don't know. I don't know how many we were at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were all civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that gathered you and selected you, the specific seven or eight civilians -- Can you please wait until I finish the question. Who was it that selected you, that went about town, as it were, and picked out civilians to carry food up to Srdj? Who was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was no one in particular. It was no one who selected us. People just came by and volunteered. They would bring the food there in a van and then they would ask the civilians who were passing by. Some people agreed to do it and some didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would you report to and where in order to assume this task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just walking by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Walking by where? Can you specify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Glavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at Ilijina Glavica, that's where you found someone who told you to take food up to Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Or, rather, no. He didn't tell us, he asked us if we could do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us specifically who was it that asked you at Ilijina Glavica to take food up to Srdj, to carry food up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some military authority or other. I can't really say who.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a military official, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suppose. I suppose so. I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At Ilijina Glavica there's a post office there, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any pine trees in the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around the post office, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. At Ilijina Glavica near the post office. Is there a green area nearby with trees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not around the post office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, further down, towards the hotel perhaps. Whatever its name is at Pile, Bogisica Park. That's further down towards the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Ilijina Glavica? What about Ilijina Glavica? Were there any Croatian artillery positions there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take that route very often on your way from Gruz to the Old Town, that's past Ilijina Glavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear sounds of firing from those places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is Bogisica Park in relation to Ilijina Glavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's nearer the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the distance between Ilijina Glavica to Bogisica Park?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I how should I know? 500 metres?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much further from Bogisica Park to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's just around the corner from Bogisica Park. You have the hotel and then the Pile Gate, the Pile area, and then the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of metres, how many metres, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, altogether perhaps two kilometres. Two kilometres, perhaps two and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Bogisica Park to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said from Ilijina Glavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my question is about the distance between Bogisica Park and the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, I have no idea. A kilometre perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you deliver food to up on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Well, I suppose there was someone up there who was in charge back then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the soldiers up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not -- not really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old were you back in 1991 when the whole thing began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- well, how old? Twenty -- 28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were 28 and you still knew no one around Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you wouldn't tell, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know those specific people. Was I supposed to know them?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take food to any other positions of the Croatian army? Please wait until I finish asking the question and then you pause and then you answer. Can you please answer now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the vehicle you used to transport food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't transport food. We walked up there, up the hill. You understand? You can't drive a vehicle up that slope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the food in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those crates, whatever. Bread in sacks, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tonci Skocko, what was his assignment in October and November and December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not assigned anywhere. He worked at the shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His father says he didn't want to leave Dubrovnik for Zagreb and that he wanted to stay and defend Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure what his father said. You should ask him perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. This is a fact not in evidence at this point. There's a proper way of leading this evidence, and I submit this is not the way to lead it. It should come through the father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll move on to a different question, but it is quite true that I did not quote from Mato Skocko's statement, but I don't think it was a misinterpretation on my part necessarily. But I will move on, however.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, Tonci's father was the manager at that shop, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this shop privately or socially owned at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the Mediator private company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who owned this private company?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please just repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirko Obrvan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers in the Old Town came to your shop to get their supplies, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I'm not sure what you mean about soldiers and supplies and my shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers who were in the Old Town, did they come to your shop to buy things? Did they come into your shop to buy something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps they were if they were on leave, if they had time off to get bread or cigarettes or whatever. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly they were not forbidden from buying in your shop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As I said, if they were free to move about, probably they would come around our shop too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they usually buy from you? What did you keep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By then, before the boats started coming, there was no electricity, no water, and we hardly had anything to keep. We had some canned food and whatever we could get from the other shops that we had in Lapad and in Gruz, and from there we would take goods to the Old Town. There were cans of food, perhaps some drinks, fruit juice, cigarettes, the bread that we brought there every morning, but the quantities were decreasing on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the soldiers then buy the canned food and fruit juice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I suppose, perhaps for their family and themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes give them stuff for free and told them that they were not supposed to pay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was not the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those soldiers put up? Please, please. Can you just hold on a second until I finish asking the question. Are you angry perhaps or something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, no. Just ask away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question is about the soldiers who came to your shop to buy things. Where were they put up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were perhaps soldiers on home leave, because they were not staying in the Old Town. Perhaps they had homes in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of those soldiers who lived inside the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a single name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I do, but why should I tell you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just to verify if your memory is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the reason for you not to -- not to want to mention these names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I should talk about these people's names. I think we should respect their privacy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're afraid to mention any specific names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again I must ask you to wait until I finish asking my question and then you can provide an answer. Are you afraid to mention any names of Croatian soldiers from that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why is it that you don't want to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I just don't. Personally, I'm not willing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you refuse to tell us other information in relation to the Croatian army in Dubrovnik then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm just not prepared to speak about these things. If you ask me about other things, I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how then can we trust you by half? You don't want to speak about the names of Croatian soldiers, but you can tell us about other things that are related to the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll tell you what I think is important, but I don't think these soldiers' names are really relevant to this Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your answers you take it upon yourself to distinguish what is important and what isn't?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think I know what's important to be said in front of this Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone draw your attention to these things prior to your testimony? Did anyone tell you what you were supposed to speak about and what not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I wasn't really ready for these questions, so that's why I'm reluctant to speak about these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which questions were you prepared for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what I came here for; the 6th of December. I was not prepared or briefed, but I'm supposed to tell the story of what happened in the town on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that briefed you or prepared you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one. I prepared myself for this testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us at least one Croatian soldier whom you saw in your shop in the Old Town where you worked or whom you saw in the street? What did one Croatian soldier look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A person with a head, with legs, with arms, with eyes, just like any other human being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you -- could you tell that he was a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he would be wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What armaments would he have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not carry any arms in Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see a single person with a rifle in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the Old Town, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would they place the weapons when they entered the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any rifle racks at the entrance to the Old Town where one would deposit one's weapons prior to going into the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there weren't, but perhaps they would leave them at their positions or wherever they felt it was needed. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a soldier leave his rifle just like that, any place during a war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know it was specifically forbidden by the police for weapons to be introduced into the Old Town, as well as by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any person in charge who had issued this prohibition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police. And of course they -- probably they had their own commander who had issued this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would at times the police perhaps arrest a soldier who was brandishing a weapon in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether the civilian police would have. Of course there were both police there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the military police then? Was it on duty controlling these things in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were only two entry gates. I mean, there was nothing to control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no civilian and military police deployed in order to maintain law and order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were there, walking about Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the civilian police armed, was the military police armed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, it's getting more consistently the case that each of you are coming in too quickly and making it difficult for the interpreter, particularly Mr. Jovic. If you would wait, when Mr. Rodic is asking a question, for a little pause before you answer. Often I can see you think of an answer before the question is quite finished, and you immediately come in with it, and that is creating a problem because it's too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you, Your Honour. We'll try again to slow things down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my last question was: The military police and the civilian police, were they armed in Old Town as people in charge of controlling law and order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and they had their arms, standard police arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of armaments are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, probably pistols and what have you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there military policemen who carry rifles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes, yes, sometimes no. Sometimes they had small rifles, sometimes a pistol and a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any members of the military police force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there perhaps on the military police force people who resided in the Old Town and were familiar with the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps there were. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where, then, were these military police and civilian police housed in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depended on their respective houses, where they lived. Some would come there. Some would be on duty. It depends on the particular case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a building in the Old Town where they had their headquarters from which their shifts would be rotated because no one could be on duty for hours on end, for 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. The civilian police was -- and I don't know where the military police was. Perhaps it was the Hotel Neptun, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the military police and civilian police go on patrols through city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They -- they patrolled the Old City.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say patrol, I mean whether they went in pairs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, usually it was in pairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any special police in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear perhaps that some members of the special police force were accommodated in Old Town and some of them at Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Definitely not -- none of them were accommodated in Stari Grad, in the Old Town, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you heard of the Sokol unit of the Croatian Party of Rights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sokol?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any members of the HOS that you came across in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how they were distinguished from other soldiers. Perhaps there were some. Perhaps by some insignia that I really didn't care to look at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any conflicts in Dubrovnik between the HOS and the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you heard nothing of the kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what positions of -- in Old Town were there sentries manned by soldiers, sentry posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Old Town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were none. At least, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the entrances and exits to and from the Old City, you didn't see any soldiers standing guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were policemen. They patrolled the city. They were patrolling the Stradun, and they were there at certain points in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there not any soldiers standing guard at the Rector's Palace and at the town hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no soldiers. It was the police. It was the reserve police force that was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these reservists, reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were on duty there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they on duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There, in the town hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning inside the municipal building, the town hall? I was asking about the security in front of the building. Was anyone securing the building in front of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them were there there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps one or two. It depended. It varied. As far as I could tell, there were one or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how could you tell? How could you see when they were inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the door was open at all times during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, that is to say from October to December 1991, did you ever go inside that building at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The town hall building?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, the Rector's Palace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us on what business you went inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that we took some merchandise from the shop in there on several occasions. Toilet paper and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I presume -- I suppose you also brought food there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- it was just toilet paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, to the best of my recollection. Perhaps some cleaning stuff as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered these things from the municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably the lady's secretary or whoever was employed there and who was in charge of such things. They would order these things by telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Crisis Staff was there as well. Weren't their needs larger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the Old Town, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, it was in the building of what is now the power distribution authority building that was above the Vila Palma, above the police building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Pero Poljanic in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the president of the Crisis Staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Pero Poljanic sitting in the town hall near the Rector's Palace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. He may have been there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zeljko Sikic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Sikic was there most of the time. In fact, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Zeljko Sikic most of the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why have you stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Nikola Obuljen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any guards near the aquarium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I never went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are Ploce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ploce are at the south exit from the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any ammunition kept there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Ploce?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear perhaps that this was a safe place for it and that that is why it was being kept there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Ploce? I don't know why. In fact, I don't know at all where ammunition was being kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mato Valjalo from the town hall who drove Zeljko Sikic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the name but I don't know that he drove him, that he was his driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at the end of the October or in early November you witnessed an attack on Dubrovnik from land and from battleships, from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. gunboats at sea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was this lengthy attack which lasted some five or six days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw the area of Lapad and Babin Kuk. Can you tell me from which point you were observing this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on that occasion the hotels Kompas, Plakir, Park and Palace were hit, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Not only these places but a number of private houses in Babin Kuk, and a couple of civilians were also killed or, rather, three or four civilians got killed in Babin Kuk, in their private home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, and I am primarily interested in hotels, that is why I'm stressing them, tell me, did you see this while the attack was going on or after the buildings were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for the Hotel Kompas and the Hotel Park, they -- I can see them directly up to the area where the Hotel Splendid is, and I cannot see the Hotel Neptun. This is quite far, but these two first ones I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning that you observed this as the fire was being opened during the operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croatian army, did it succeed in repelling the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. The attack lasted for about five or six days, the most intense portion of the attack. And then I heard on the news, and it was in the papers, some sort of a cease-fire had been signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian military nearby around those hotels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean those hotels over there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were positions up there at the fort on top of Babin Kuk, but I'm not sure if there were any other positions or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone firing from there? Was anyone defending?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, I didn't see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it can't be the case, can it, that in all of five days no one was firing back from the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at least to the extent that I was able to see there was nothing like that. Now, what anyone else was doing, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it was in that period of time that some Croatian military were put up at the Stadion Hotel, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That period of time, I don't know. I wasn't there at the time, so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, whose headquarters were at the Kompas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one's headquarters. The Kompas Hotel, I think those were only civilian refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the Kompas Hotel, was there a base for Croatian naval boats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Kompas and Neptun Hotels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Lapad inlet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Croatian war boats were there at Lapad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see any boats there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not then. Not at the time. It was later in March when I was on my way to Kalamota that that was our departure point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those hydrofoils, were those used to transport people? Were reinforcements being brought in from Ston, were they used for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Mato from the port authorities who drove a hydrofoil like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the diving instructor from the local club, the one who didn't have a leg? He also drove a hydrofoil. Did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I know one, a man with a beard who drove. He was a bit older. I don't know what he was specifically, but he drove a hydrofoil, but that was later, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was movement restricted in the area of the Palace Hotel, Vila Rasica. The town hospital, and Gorica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with that. But I don't believe so because there were hotels brimming with refugees there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this area I've just mentioned, were there any Croatian military in this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, up there where they were stationed, at Vila Rasica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any artillery positions there, a self-propelled machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not an objection. I'd just ask my learned friend to specify when. When he's asking the witness questions about various things like this, that he actually specifies when he's referring to; otherwise it's particularly vague in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that could be useful, Mr. Rodic. We've spanned quite a time in the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, except for when I specified the dates, all the questions I ask are in relation to the period between October and December 1991. My questions are always about that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that hasn't been clear until now. So the answers may not have reflected that to now, but we'll keep that in mind for the future, Mr. Rodic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those five days that you refer to during the attack, you said that the warehouse at the Gruz port had burned down, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Jadranko Delas from the municipal Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Delas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Dubrovkinja lorries were used to transfer weapons and ammunition over from Ploce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that there were weapons being stored between link 8 and link 9 at the warehouse in Gruz and that this was what burnt down during the attack on the Gruz harbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't know this. As for the Gruz harbour, I know that it was on fire, but wooden structures such as warehouses were burning. I'm not sure what was in those. Coffee stored, perhaps. There was a huge freezer with bananas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I understand, coffee and bananas can't just explode like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not saying that they exploded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't hear any explosions in the harbour itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Able-bodied men, were they allowed to leave Dubrovnik? 1st of October until the 31st of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think they were allowed to leave. I think one needed to apply for a special permit from the Crisis Staff to leave the town of Dubrovnik. Those who were ill perhaps later on were taken on ships in mid-December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, able-bodied men were supposed to obtain a special permit from the Crisis Staff if they wanted to leave the area of Dubrovnik town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who specifically in the Crisis Staff was in charge of issuing this permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't apply for one myself, therefore I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where specifically did you go to get one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, I think the Crisis Staff headquarters were at the Electroprivreda building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of issuing those permits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Tonci Skocko lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Zlatni Potok.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Captain Cengija? Didn't he hold positions there for a while?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. No, no, not there. Those were residential buildings. Maybe further up behind the Belvedere Hotel. That's where the positions were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Captain Cengija was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe he's actually a general, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about Aziz Suljevic from the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was a commander of the military police, wasn't he? But I'm not sure. I heard the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about Dajdza?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was back in Cepikuce as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later in the Dubrovnik area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think he was there but I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Zoran Primic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Primic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was there at the Zagreb Hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the 1st of October and the 31st of December.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Nojko Marinovic? Was he there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know or you're not supposed to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. He didn't really show civilians around and show them where he lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Kreso Mandic who was the commander of the special police at Plato [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He used to work as a driver for Djuro Korda.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Stjepan Medjat [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Medjat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I've ever heard that name. Perhaps a similar one but not that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nojko Marinovic's driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this would be a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, in addition to those days that you mentioned, the days in October, November, and December 1991 when the shop was closed, your shop, when it was closed, and you described the reasons, between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, did you go to work in the Old Town all the time to work at the shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, except for the four days or five days at the beginning and another five or six days in November and the 6th, 7th, and 8th of December. Aside from that, I went to work all the time. On the 6th I was there at the shop, but not on the 7th or 8th. That's when the shop was closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you leave home, when you leave Gruz and you go to work, you go to the Old Town. Can you describe the route you usually take.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would go down to the port in Gruz first. That's where the driver lived who drove the van that we used to transport bread. So I would drive together with him. We would stop by the bakery and then drive past Ilijina Glavica and Zlatni Potok and on to the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't think I understood. You drive past Ilijina Glavica and then where do you go next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we go to the area that is usually referred to as Kapelica, and then down past the fire brigade building where the funicular is, and then you take a roundabout route past Zlatni Potok, and then you reach the town gates so you can drive into the town with a van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you drive through the Pile Gate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. You never drive through the Pile Gate. That's not the direction you need to take if you want to drive into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned this van, do you mean the vehicle you described as a caddy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This type of vehicle, is it a Golf caddy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was -- what's the name? Zastava 101, a small pick-up. It was closed at the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This van, this pick-up truck, which gate did you use to enter the old town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Ploce Gate. We drove through the Ploce Gate. That's the gate we took. That's where we came in and that's where we came out also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you get there? Which road do you take to get there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, to the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, you take the roundabout road through Zlatni Potok, because that's where the road takes you, and then past the Excelsior Hotel, and then you reach the Ploce Gate. That's a one-way road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- did you drive over a pontoon, a bridge to reach the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's not really a pontoon bridge. It's just a bridge at the gate. Just outside the gate. It's an old bridge. It's been there for the last 10.000 years, since 1.000 -- I can't remember when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to those stairs you were talking about, where did you leave the vehicle? Where did you park it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The driver would drive back, would just unload the bread, and then the driver would go back near the Rector's Palace, and then we would use some sort of a cart to -- to transport these goods to the shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period when you went to work regularly, did you hear a general alert being sounded in Dubrovnik, the siren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it always sounded when the town was fired on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, almost always. As soon as there was firing on the town. I mean the town, I mean Lapad, I mean Gruz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what would people do once the alarm was sounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first everyone would run to the shelters. There were few shelters. And later on, people would just take shelter wherever they were, in their private houses, or if the house had a cellar. Those who felt safe where they were just stayed there. Some people went to the shelter, and some people were at work and couldn't leave. They would come to the shop, for example. A general alert had been sounded, so they would just stay where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to -- to any of the shelters during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in the Old Town. As I said, we felt that the Old Town would not come under attack. It wasn't only me. We all felt safer in the Old Town. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the exception of the 6th of December, you said that in October, two shells had landed on the Old Town. That's what you said, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said those two shells fell on Miha Pracata Street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was that street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that no one was wounded on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About the general alert, when the general alert is sounded and the firing begins, when you were at the shop, in terms of its size, did you feel safe there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't feel safe in the shop, but we felt safer because we were in the Old Town, after all, and we thought that the Old Town would not be targeted. We were convinced, because it was a UNESCO World Heritage Site, that the Old Town would not be targeted. So that many people who lived inside the Old Town felt the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there people inside the Old Town who, as soon as the general alert was sounded, ran to the shelters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite many of the people, in fact. There were elderly people, too, who even slept in shelters. They were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 6th of December when the firing began, was the alarm sounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The siren went off early in the morning, at about 6:00 in the morning, I believe, as soon as the first shells started landing on the town, on Lapad, on Gruz, at about 6:00, half past six in the morning. Even before shells started landing on the Old Town, the general alert had been sounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about those two shells in October, the shells that landed in Miha Pracata Street? Do you know where exactly those two shells landed? Was there any damage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One fell on the pavement, and I think one was lodged inside the stone facade of one of the buildings there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which street number specifically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those five days in November when you said there was a lot of shelling, where did you stay during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Back at my place in Gruz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After those five days, you went back to work regularly, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no changes or damage to the Old Town at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, except for those two shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those two we said had landed in October; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One thing I forgot to ask you when we spoke about the 163rd Brigade of the Croatian army, who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was there, I think the commander was Nojko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of the 116th Brigade of the ZNG, the National Guard Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many of these numbers, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many numbers? How many different brigades were there, roughly speaking, in the Dubrovnik area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were none before the 31st of December. At least, the 163 was not there because it had not been established yet. I think it was only established as late as January or February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about elements of the 114th and 116th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't think they were deployed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What military units were there in October, November, and December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the only thing that was there was the National Guard Corps at Vila Rasica. I'm not sure how many people exactly, but there could not have been a lot of people. I think 200 at the most. There were those civilians who were part of the civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any armed people with -- carrying infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were those soldiers carrying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rifles. Because at that time it was hard to tell. One could not distinguish. All these were actually civilians. There were few soldiers. All of these were civilians who lived in houses to defend their homes. If you met a person with a rifle, you knew that that person was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning that there were also civilians who were carrying weapons, in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the lack of uniforms, this means that there were people wearing civilian clothes who were also carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Initially I believe all of them were like that, because there were no uniforms. With this exception of the National Guard Corps. The Territorial Defence members, some of them wore the former JNA uniforms, perhaps just the trousers or the boots, and then they would place a different insignia as a mark of distinction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were the mortar positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct what you've just said that the positions of the JNA at -- on land were Osojnik, Mokosica, Orasac, Rozat, all the way up to Sustjepan, Brgat, Bosanka, a part of the Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were the Croatian positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them were down there, as far as I can remember, at the Kantafig at the exit from Gruz, Sustjepan, Srdj, near the Hotel Belvedere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around the Hotel Belvedere was this the last line of defence of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was housed there? What was located there at the Belvedere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, just the army. I don't see how anything else could have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was there any artillery there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear in the region of Dubrovnik that the Croatian army had any mortars or cannon or the like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, I believe that the only thing they had as far as I had heard was -- that was up there at the Gradac Park, they had some, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will Ms. Usher please present to the witness Defence Exhibit number 31. If -- given our time constraints, if you also could be so kind as to prepare D28, 32, and 35, and P24, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this section of the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot find my feet here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you associate this with the -- with the Bogisica Park?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. The forest perhaps can be a link, but I don't know from which position this shot was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please then show the witness photograph D28. Can we have a colour photograph, please. Are these marks are actually D, Defence. So it's D28, D31, D32, D35. So Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photograph tells me nothing really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This civilian --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fail to see anything much. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you then show the witness the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer to the Gradac Park. You said that you heard that there were artillery positions there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I said was that perhaps there were mortars there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a cannon, a gun in Gradac Park. Did you ever hear of a gun being there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. And this photograph could have been taken anywhere or of anyplace. It doesn't really tell one it's precisely Gradac Park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us then take a look at the following, at the next photograph. Did you ever see a three-barrelled gun, a truck-mounted three-barrelled gun there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that there existed a truck-mounted three-barrel gun there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that the mortar had been positioned or, rather, mounted upon a truck in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I no longer need those photographs. Can we now have Prosecution Exhibit P24, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second photograph down here. Did you ever see this armoured personnel carrier, this armoured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw it at the very beginning the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was using it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As this person -- it is, rather, armed with a heavy machine-gun. Do you know at what positions it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recognise this location where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps near the Vila Palma where the police is, but I'm not sure. I cannot say with precision really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You can return the photograph. Do you know who was the head of the police department in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just give me a minute. I'll try to recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I remind you, was it perhaps not Djuro Korda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the armaments and military equipment at the Vila Palma?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that. The police was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in front of the Vila Palma, were there any anti-aircraft, three-barrelled guns, namely the gun which used to be mounted on the police patrol boat near Srdj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian troops at the Hotel Dubrovnik President?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Hotel Dubrovnik President at Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't believe so, because this was in Babin Kuk and in Minceta I know there were refugees, and in Plakir and Argos. I believe that in all the hotels there were refugees. Perhaps not at the President because it is the most seaward hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the Hotel Neptun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no refugees at the Hotel Neptun, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about refugees. I'm asking about soldiers and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and units in and around the hotel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Hotel Petka in Gruz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the zone Hotel Neptun, the Solitudo camp and the Kompas Hotel, were there any troops there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps at the Neptun Hotel -- by the Neptun Hotel there were some. I don't know about the other ones. In Kompas I don't know. In Solitudo, I don't know. Perhaps down there at the beach or somewhere thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the Montovjerna zone were there emplacements of mortars and anti-aircraft guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These positions were dug in in only 1992, I know that, and that was later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Gradac near the Radio Dubrovnik building, were there any pieces of artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the zone called the Chinese Wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is in Lapad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any positions there, army positions?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there mortars in Pile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there weren't. Because I pass there every day and I didn't notice any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you passed by the opposite end, the one in Ploce.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but of course when one came to town one had to go through this gate to go to Buninovo. There was no other way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at Pile near the bus roundabout, was there one of the ZNG headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Pile? No. No, where the buses turn, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And near the old people's home, were there any Croatian soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the town, in the Old Town, or up there near Buninovo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that there were none in the Old Town. As for the other place, I don't think there were any there either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there elements of the Croatian navy in Batale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Batala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't believe so. Batala is right next to the stadium and the bus station down there. This is an inlet in the Gruz harbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there ZNG members near the Libertas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Passing through town, did you ever see bunkers established there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the Old City, the Old Town, or the city of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, by the post office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which post office?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Outside the Old City.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But there are five of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you take your road home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Glavica, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the Hotel Petka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A bunker? No, I didn't see one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I say a bunker. It doesn't have to be a built pillbox. What I mean, it can be a structure like a sandbag, something of the kind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, these are not bunkers. We had a shelter erected in our own building so that people could take shelter there in the cellar. Now, if that considered to be a bunker, then we had one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I gave it the wrong term. What I was talking about are such positions which were militarily regulated and where there were soldiers; for instance, near the access to the main road near the health centre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is near Glavica, up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't go up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in front of the electrical power authority building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the city market.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're talking about the one in Gruz or the one in town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards Gruz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is one at the station. Where? Which one are you referring to? Did you see any one established near any petrol station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the Adriatic Hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I never went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any such arranged positions, for instance, with sandbags anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did see such positions, but only later. At Kantafig, at the exit there under the bridge, at the exit from Gruz. Not in the town itself, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "later," when was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean later in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When in 1992? Early?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Later, May or June, after the army had withdrawn from Mokosica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you spent most of the days inside the Old Town between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, did you ever hear or see firing by the Croatian artillery from inside Dubrovnik, this period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the 31st of December, you mean. Well, the only thing I heard was up on Srdj, thereabouts, Sustjepan, around Belvedere, about -- no -- yes, Belvedere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that artillery fire you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You heard explosions. Everyone was shooting. It was difficult to say whether it was artillery fire or something else. There were shoot-outs with bullets, hand-to-hand combat, rifle fire. That was the most frequent sound on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From both sides rifle fire was the most frequent sound you heard; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was practically non-stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P75, P75.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a UNESCO flag looks like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a white flag with a coat of arms, some sort of escutcheon inside on it, the UNESCO sign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the flag or emblem that you referred that had been displayed on certain buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was it went like this and it went like that and it said "Monument of Culture" in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also white.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just white.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness indicated something -- I could see from this angle, indicated something on the table in front of him. Perhaps that could be described for the record. The "It went like this and went like that" bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were you pointing to something on the map there, Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can draw it for you on a slip of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need, Your Honour. Maybe this can be used on redirect if this needs verifying. I would like to move on now, if I can, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please display on the ELMO, so we can all see, your own markings. Well, actually, it's clear enough. A -- if we can just zoom in every so slightly, please. This building that you marked as A, that's your shop; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the letter B marks the spot where Tonci Skocko and you were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The arrow in front of the letter B is the direction you were facing. You were facing the Stradun, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Behind you is this point just behind the letter B. There's an arrow and the letter C marking the spot. This marks the spot where the shell landed, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, roughly speaking the letter B, okay, but it was within a radius of ten metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know we can't attain for very high degrees of accuracy if we're using this map, but roughly speaking, I want to know if you can tell me, please, in relation to this position marked as B, the shell landed about ten metres behind where you were standing. Am I correct in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One fell just in front and one fell behind us. The first one -- the one that was behind was the one which fell first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please point it out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one that is marked in black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which was the shell that caused your injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one that fell lower down, the second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which one is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This second arrow lower down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please point it out to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how much time elapsed between those two shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, 15, 20 minutes perhaps. Perhaps even less. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you spent those 15 or 20 minutes just standing there in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or you came out twice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. I said the first shell fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which was the first shell? Can you please show that on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The one marked in black. The first shell fell. It ricochetted and then it smashed the window and the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. So when the first shell fell, it fell about ten metres from the building marked as A. At that point in time you were not standing outside in the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. But it was outside the building marked as A, in the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that first shell landed, did you come out to see where it had fallen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That's not why we came out but, rather, one of the customers, as I said, came in and said that the house marked as D was on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where the shelter was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was just across the way from -- from the house marked as D, the elementary school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show us on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's where the shelter was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the elementary school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The elementary school building and the shelter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a music school nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's -- that's further up the street. It would be about this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the music school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So within that circle we have the music school, and where the letter D is, that's the house across the way from the elementary school; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
