utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 15 or 20 minutes that elapsed between the two shells, as you said, did you leave the building to go outside the shop again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just that once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the time when you went out, how much time had elapsed before the second shell landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were you from your shop when the second shell landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's all on the stairs outside the shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you standing exactly outside the door or did you perhaps move towards the building marked as D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We faced the same way as the building marked as A. We were standing right there next to that building, on the staircase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far from the door of the building marked as A were you standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps one and a half or two metres. The street itself is not much wider than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A metre and a half or two towards the building marked as D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. If you face directly across. So it was around here, on this street. That's how big the street is, and that's where we were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that morning, did you leave the shop a number of times to see where the shells were falling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we didn't. Not in the morning. We were working. We were selling bread and whatever we had in the shop, and customers kept coming in. After 7:00, no one came, after the shells had started falling on the town. All you could hear were explosions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone move in the direction of the music school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Perhaps I saw one man when the house was on fire after we come out. There was a person who ran across the street to the shelter. Like this. This is the house where the person entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the police question you about the injuries you sustained, your injuries, and the wounding of Tonci Skocko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone question Tonci Skocko's father in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if an on-site investigation was carried out after Tonci Skocko's killing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you at least roughly determine the time when this happened in the morning, the wounding and the death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole thing began at about 7:00. It may have been about 8.00 or 9.00, half past nine perhaps, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Pavo Djivanovic from Ljuta? He was born in 1959.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name rings a bell, but I can't quite --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Vlaho Momkovic from Ljuta, who lives in Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you had worked together for a long time, did you socialise with Tonci Skocko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tonci started working with us back in 1991, I believe, early summer. We would visit him at his home in Ljuta, his father's home, his father Mato, for a while, but we didn't really socialise. There was a barbecue that we organised there. It was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tonci mention these two people as friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He may have, but it's difficult for me to remember now. Maybe he did and maybe he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tonci resided at Zlatni Potok, number 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number, but he did reside at Zlatni Potok.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain why in this report on the external examination of dead bodies dated the 7th of November, 1991, this report was compiled on behalf of the investigating magistrate of the district court with crime technicians and police inspectors present, why does it say that Tonci Skocko was killed near the music school which is in a totally different area from the one you pointed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure why that's what is stated there. It was all nearby, so perhaps people just put down the wrong place. Someone said something about the music school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance between the music school and your shop, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 13 or 14 metres [as interpreted], perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say 30 or 40 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what Tonci Skocko wore on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a jersey, long sleeves. Well, now, probably he had pants on him. I don't know. I no longer remember. It's been a long time. I know he had this jersey that he had wrapped around himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With buttons or a different kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just an ordinary jersey. Perhaps with a few buttons here on top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps not. Trousers, a tracksuit, shoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we say "trousers," you mean jeans, trousers, something like that? You say pants colloquially, and then probably training shoes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of the clothes he wore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you said that you personally carried him into the vehicle and that the clothes got caught in the door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the jersey in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The jersey. What was the colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was yellowish, but it's -- it's been such a long time. I don't think I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone show you a photograph of the body of the late Tonci Skocko later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that he had been hit in the heart by a piece of shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you noticed a small injury on his body which you described as the size of a grain of corn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe where exactly this injury was located on the body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the chest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which side; left or right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The right half, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although general alert had been sounded that morning on account of the shelling, you, as I understand, left the shop, went outside the shop, and you were smoking outside the shop, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid you got it wrong. What I said is that when we arrived in town at 6:00 or half past six, the general alert had been sounded, and then later there was firing on the Old Town and shells started falling. So no one came to the shop after that. It's only the few people who were already there. Those people stayed. And when I say we went outside, yes, we may have gone outside for a minute or two to light a cigarette or something like that. We may have been outside for just a brief while when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it not risky during a general alert and after you'd heard a shell fall nearby on Miha Pracata Street for you to leave the shop and smoke outside in the street unprotected like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Sure, it was risky. It happened, and I still feel guilty about it. I felt guilty about it for a long time afterwards.
